rv.q: I came out feeling I had seen a pleasantly humane play but one that tied up life's problems with too neat and bright a ribbon.
The pleasures of the produc- tion-which, incidentally. none of the five NT companies seems anxious to claim-are minor and rooted in Simon's rhythmic, idiomatic turns Qf phrase.

Sure, Simon inclines to comedy where Miller inclined his family to tragedy; but in his own memory of himself at fifteen, Simonhascomeupwithatouching anc! marvellous narrator, a coher- ent American Adrian Mole whose diary is a mixture of random guilt and delighted sexual awakening.
Unfortunately after the interval despite Rudman's sensitive and lively interpretation - the balance goes all wrong.

cn.t: Neil Simon's autobiographical comedy earns praise for its charm, craftsmanship, and dexterous construction, with Michael Rudman's National Theatre production achieving a transatlantic breakthrough that improves upon the Broadway original.
